question: Methylphenidate is the first-line pharmacological agent for ADHD in school-age children when medication is indicated, and it should always be used as part of a multimodal plan that includes behavioural therapy and psychoeducation rather than as a standalone treatment.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Methylphenidate is the established first-line stimulant medication for ADHD in school-age children. It must be embedded within a multimodal plan — the MTA trial demonstrated that combined pharmacological and behavioural treatment is superior to medication alone. Prescribing methylphenidate without behavioural and psychoeducational support is suboptimal practice.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Methylphenidate (a CNS stimulant acting on dopamine and noradrenaline reuptake) is the first-line pharmacological agent for ADHD in children aged 6 years and above when medication is indicated. Evidence from the landmark MTA trial and subsequent studies consistently shows that combined treatment (medication + behavioural therapy) produces better outcomes than either alone, and psychoeducation of parents and teachers is a core component.
